claim: As VOC Ceylon became more territorially and fiscally intrusive, registration, litigation and social categorisation increased the colonial state's legibility of land, people and service obligations.
bounded_by: The two supporting works are distinct scholarly works but share the Cambridge publishing domain. Treat this as bounded same-publisher corroboration until an independent archival or scholarly source family is added; do not generalize uniformly across all provinces or periods.
notes: Do not recast this as a uniform top-down invention of fixed ethnic identities; categorisation was negotiated and institution-specific.
